Bureaucracy ( / b j ʊəˈr ɒ k r ə s i / ⓘ bure- OK -rə-see ) is a system of organization where laws or regulatory authority are implemented by civil servants (non-elected officials). [ 1 ] Historically, a bureaucracy was a government administration managed by departments staffed with non-elected officials. [ 2 ] Today, bureaucracy is the administrative system governing any large institution, whether publicly owned or privately owned. [ 3 ] The public administration in many jurisdictions is an example of bureaucracy, as is any centralized hierarchical structure of an institution, including corporations , societies , nonprofit organizations , and clubs .
